 'Kind of cool': Early Anthropic investor and actor Ashton Kutcher celebrates IPO
 Grace O'Donnell · Editor, Special Projects Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:01 PM PST 3 min read ANT +11.57% 
 Ashton Kutcher celebrated Anthropic's ( ANT ) blockbuster IPO on Thursday, and with good reason: Sound Ventures, the venture capital firm Kutcher co-founded, made a $435 million investment in Anthropic that's now worth roughly $7 billion. 
 With Anthropic now worth well over $1 trillion in market capitalization, Kutcher's stake could push the "That '70s Show" actor toward becoming a billionaire, according to Newsweek . 
 "People usually see the one deal and think that's the whole thing, but the ones who know realize that it's years of work, micro victories and failures stacked on top of one another," Kutcher wrote on X. 
 "Kind of cool when that works out," Kutcher added. 
 Kutcher began Sound Ventures with Guy Oseary, a talent manager for stars like Madonna, 11 years ago. The firm was the successor to Kutcher and Oseary's first VC firm, A-Grade Investments, which was founded in 2010. 
 The group began investing in Anthropic in 2023 and later built up a 0.5% stake in the Claude creator. 
 "I see [Dario Amodei] no different than one of the greatest musicians who's got all of these ideas in their minds, and they're going to go in the studio and make an incredible album," Oseary told Bloomberg in a recent interview . "This might be one of the greatest debut albums of all time." 
 On Thursday, Anthropic began trading on the public markets for the first time, raising a record-breaking $81 billion. The stock opened 34% above its IPO price at a valuation of $1.5 trillion.

 Sound Ventures has also invested in OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) and Fei-Fei Li's World Labs, which was r ecently acquired by Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) for $8.2 billion. 
 Interestingly, the Wall Street Journal reported in July that Kutcher was leaving Sound Ventures to start a separate VC fund with Morgan Beller. However, Kutcher will continue to serve as an adviser to the firm, TechCrunch reported. 
 Sound Ventures has not disclosed Kutcher's stake in the VC firm, and it's not known whether his departure affected his right to share in Anthropic's IPO windfall. 
 "Congrats to our team that helped us craft and execute a vision," Kutcher wrote. "And thank you to those who didn't believe in us. You made us work harder."
